lines.text: Father, in the name of Jesus, we pray for every son, every daughter.
Give them the heart to trust You and hold on to Your promise.
So that they’ll know that as a Father, You’ll never go back on Your promises.
And again, we pray for our fathers. Every father who has not kept their promise,
help them begin to live a life where they trust in You first, as the promise keeper, and hold on to You.

art.prompt: Night in a West African family compound: a long low plastered house with a rusty tin roof and a shaded veranda, a big mango tree, a few plastic chairs against the wall. On the right third of the frame a boy of about ten in a brown polo shirt, with a steel wristwatch on his wrist, sits alone on a low wooden bench, an empty enamel bowl beside him after his evening meal. He tilts his head back and looks up at the sky with a small calm smile, his right hand raised with one finger pointing up as he counts the stars. Above the dark mango tree the deep teal night sky is full of bright stars. One warm light bulb glows under the veranda behind him and lights the side of his face. Large calm empty starry sky on the left. The mood is safe, quiet and wondering.

First light of dawn, long ago, in the stone courtyard of the temple in Jerusalem; the sky above is still deep teal with the last stars fading. On the right third of the frame a very old man with a long white beard, in a simple cream robe with a striped shawl over his head, is seen from behind and slightly to the side so his face is not visible; he holds a tiny newborn baby wrapped completely in white cloth close against his shoulder, and lifts his head toward the sky in thanks. The baby is fully swaddled and its face is hidden in the cloth against his shoulder. A few steps behind him, small and seen from behind, a young mother in a blue head covering and a carpenter in a brown robe stand watching. Warm golden rays of the rising sun pour between tall stone columns and fall on the old man and the baby. Large calm empty area of soft golden light and pale stone on the left.

Night inside a small one-room home with deep teal walls. On the left third of the frame a West African father in a green patterned shirt, a steel wristwatch on his wrist, sits on a low wooden stool beside his son's sleeping mat on the floor, home as he promised, one hand resting gently on the shoulder of his sleeping son. The boy, about seven, in a yellow shirt, sleeps peacefully under a plain, unpatterned cream cotton cloth with a small smile; the cloth and the pillow are plain, with no writing, labels, stripes or print of any kind. A pair of new black school shoes sits neatly side by side at the foot of the mat. A single candle burns on a low wooden table beside them, and the wooden door behind them is closed. Warm candlelight on the father's calm face and the sleeping boy; the mood is tender, quiet and safe. Large calm empty area of teal wall on the right.

shorts.post: Faithfulness means keeping your word, night after night, morning after morning. God's mercy does not run out by evening; it is new again every time the sun comes up. Lamentations 3:22–23. Full devotional on YouTube @KidsInspiringNation #TheFatherShowedUp #DailyDevotional #KidsInspiringNation #Lamentations3 #FamilyDevotion

titles: God Keeps His Promises | Day 6 · The Father Showed Up
His Mercies Are New Every Morning
When Promises Have Been Broken Before
social.description:
Maybe promises have been broken in your life before. Tonight we meet the one Father who has never broken His word: His mercies are new every morning, and He kept His biggest promise when He sent His Son.

THE WORD: Lamentations 3:22–23 (read Lamentations 3:19–26 aloud)
TONIGHT, children: start a secret count of God’s faithfulness. Each night this month, make one mark for one good thing God did.
TONIGHT, fathers: make one small promise you can really keep, and say it out loud to God. When you have kept it, mark it. Repeat tomorrow.
SAY IT: God keeps His promises. He sent His Son.
social.pinned: What is one good thing God did for you today? Write it below as your first mark, and under it write: “God keeps His promises.”
